question: Climbers who reach the top of Mount Everest are standing on rock that formed at the bottom of what?
source_excerpt: almost unmetamorphosed shallow marine Ordovician limestone that rose from the floor of the ancient Tethys Ocean to form the summit

extra.why_interesting: Players think of Everest as the most un-sea-like place on Earth: high, frozen and far from any coast. Finding out that its very top was once the seabed flips that, and players who know continents collide can reason their way there.
extra.verification_notes: Everest's summit is Ordovician marine limestone (Qomolangma Formation) deposited on the floor of the ancient Tethys sea/ocean, so 'the sea' is correct; see https://www.earthsciences.hku.hk/shmuseum/earth_evo_08_2.5.2.5.php

explanation: The summit is limestone packed with fossils of tiny sea creatures, laid down on an ancient ocean floor. When India crashed into Asia, that seabed was pushed almost nine kilometres into the sky.
